sections.title: Market Pulse: Inflation Concerns Weigh Heavily

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Retreat Amid Hotter-Than-Expected Inflation Data
items.summary: Wall Street concluded Wednesday's session mostly lower as a stronger-than-anticipated September Consumer Price Index report heightened concerns about potential Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. Financial and healthcare sectors were notable drags, while a rotation from growth to value stocks continued, revealing underlying market weakness despite the S&P 500's relatively flat close.

sections.title: Top Movers: Wednesday's Gainers and Losers

items.headline: Greenland Energy Co Surges
items.summary: Greenland Energy Co ($GLND) shares recorded an impressive 77.77% increase, closing at $3.93.

items.headline: Bending Spoons SPA Rises on Investment
items.summary: BENDING SPOONS SPA ($BSP) advanced 39.16% to $52.69 following news of Berkshire Hathaway's additional $330 million investment.

items.headline: BlackRock Boosted by Strong Earnings
items.summary: BlackRock ($BLK) rose 3.87% after the asset manager reported third-quarter profit and revenue that exceeded analyst estimates.

items.headline: CL WORKSHOP GROUP LTD Plummets
items.summary: CL WORKSHOP GROUP LTD's ($NWGL) shares dropped 77.47%, closing at $0.27.

items.headline: Bank of America Falls on Earnings Miss and Penalty
items.summary: Bank of America ($BAC) sank 5.53% after reporting a drop in third-quarter profit, missing earnings forecasts, and incurring a $1.2 billion regulatory penalty.

items.headline: Johnson & Johnson Tumbles on Revenue Miss
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson's ($JNJ) shares tumbled 5.7% after the company's revenues of $25.43 billion marginally missed analyst estimates, despite exceeding quarterly earnings.

items.headline: September CPI Hotter Than Expected, Fuels Fed Rate Hike Bets
items.summary: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.6% month-over-month in September, with the annual rate accelerating to 3.7%, exceeding economists' forecasts. Core CPI also came in hotter than anticipated at 2.6% year-over-year. This data has significantly increased investor expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month.

items.headline: Healthcare and Financials Lead Sector Decline; Energy Outperforms
items.summary: The Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) declined 1.3%, while the Financials Select Sector SPDR (XLF) fell 0.4%, pulling down broader markets. In contrast, the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) advanced 1.7%, emerging as the day's leading sector. Technology and semiconductor stocks also faced selling pressure.

items.headline: Mixed Q3 Earnings from Major Banks, JNJ Misses Revenue
items.summary: Major U.S. banks reported mixed third-quarter earnings, with Bank of America ($BAC) notably down after a profit drop and regulatory penalty. Citigroup ($C) also fell due to declining investment banking fees and higher credit-loss provisions. Johnson & Johnson ($JNJ) saw its shares tumble after revenues marginally missed estimates.

items.headline: Rising Oil Prices and Geopolitical Tensions Fuel Inflationary Concerns
items.summary: Elevated oil prices, partially attributed to the ongoing conflict in Iran, continue to contribute to inflationary pressures. Coupled with the build-out of AI infrastructure increasing demand for commodities, these macro trends are seen as significant catalysts pushing U.S. interest rates higher and creating headwinds for economic growth.
